title: perf(storage): optimize grouped directory updates, ranks and memory
body:
## Context

Splitting or removing the first page of a grouped List rebuilt its directory because later logical page ordinals shifted. Grouped ZRANK/ZREVRANK scanned ordered pages from an endpoint despite the existing member-score graph and Fenwick counts. Fixed-capacity metadata chunks and an always-resident eight-entry physical-coordinate overlay also made small grouped values unnecessarily expensive.

## Behavior before and after

List directories now keep stable physical ring slots, with an ID map and Fenwick counts over those slots. With spare capacity, end splits/removals preserve middle metadata and validate only the replaced chain interval and its boundary links. Capacity growth and length-changing middle splices may still rebuild; pops do not shrink capacity. Small Lists recover with exactly their live slot count, while larger rings reserve geometric slack.

ZRANK/ZREVRANK resolve the member's score through the member graph, search score-bounded ordered pages, and combine a Fenwick prefix with the page offset. Missing members require no ordered-page read. Rank/score range scans also use Fenwick prefixes. Equal-score runs can still span all pages.

Small CowArrays now allocate one variable-capacity shared chunk and point directly to it. Construction allocates only live entries; appends may reserve bounded tail capacity. Larger arrays use a persistent pointer tree and preserve local copying. Physical-coordinate overlays allocate only when populated. Resident ordered-page entries omit transaction IDs after recovery adjudication.

Disk formats, record IDs, physical write sets, recovery transaction selection and publication/undo protocols are unchanged.

## Implementation

- Keep List page metadata in a COW ring. One persistent ID map distinguishes live slots from append-only retirement slots. Validate changed identities, aggregates, reciprocal links, interval coverage and retirement evidence; coalesce Fenwick changes by physical slot.
- Give CowArray chunks an owner-thread intrusive header plus aligned trailing element storage. Only live elements are constructed/copied; each allocation admits and accounts its own lifetime. Unique point updates allocate nothing. Shared updates detach their path and chunk; allocation failure preserves predecessor values. Single-chunk promotion, over-aligned elements and throwing copies are covered by tests.
- Keep the default 32-entry limit for ID and Fenwick chunks. The limit bounds copying, while small chunks can have less capacity. Directory scratch stores the resident entry type directly, so CowArray needs only its ordinary span-based API.
- Store at most eight live physical overrides in one shared CowArray chunk. Empty states allocate no overlay. New coordinate views allocate an exact-size after-image; metadata-only views share it. Overflow, topology changes and external records fold into the physical index.
- Define page metadata once in the 120-byte OrderedGroupEntry. RecoveredOrderedGroup is a non-polymorphic value extension adding two decision tags (136 bytes total on this aarch64 platform). Recovery still checks both transaction IDs before selecting a winner. Incarnation, sequence, LSN, record token, links and routing bounds remain resident for existing validation and lookup paths. Readers and suffix validation borrow this common base directly, avoiding fieldwise conversions and pointer variants.
- Share envelope validation between recovery and foreground changes. A single foreground change analysis rejects duplicate/invalid identities and computes checked aggregate deltas for List and linear directories. Unchanged-topology updates share one page/Fenwick replacement implementation, while ring intervals, Stream suffixes and full-chain reconstruction retain their own reachability checks.
- Estimate CowMap allocations from the actual combined LocalSharedPtr layout, including allocator state and alignment, instead of a fixed per-node margin.
- Use validated Stream header magic as the cache-presence marker. CowArray remains 24 bytes, OrderedGroupDirectory 424 bytes, and GroupedObject 528 bytes on this platform.

## Design decisions and alternatives

A ring directly addresses List end edits while reusing CowArray, CowMap and FenwickTree. It retains spare slots after pops and uses more ID-map metadata than the old packed ID array. Large recovery/layout growth still reserves slack; exact-size recovery applies to small Lists.

The rank path adds no resident index. Ties can still make candidate-page traversal linear.

Variable-capacity chunks avoid small-value slack and the first pointer branch. Their header is slightly larger than the old fixed chunk: an 8,193-element uint64 CowArray uses 78,704 B versus 76,976 B in the previous PR revision. Removing recovery-only page fields more than offsets this for ordered metadata.

Lazy physical overlays trade memory for allocation work. Each modified immutable overlay needs a new allocation, not just the first use. Empty states save 368 B, but a fully populated eight-entry overlay uses 56 B more than the previous inline array. Local measurements below show a CPU cost, so this is not presented as a universal speedup.

## Documentation and comments

Updated the grouped-collections architecture for ring ownership/validation, member-rank lookup, variable-capacity COW storage, lazy physical overlays and recovery-only transaction tags. Nearby comments document borrowed lifetimes, admission failure, alignment, reserved slots, snapshot preservation and header-cache validity.

## Test plan

```sh
cmake --build build_debug --target lavik_unit_tests lavik lavik_grouped_recovery_e2e_test lavik_grouped_ordered_write_e2e_test --parallel 6

build_debug/lavik_unit_tests --gtest_filter='*Group*:*CowMap*:*FenwickTree*:*Ordered*:*SortedRewrite*:*StreamDirectory*:*StreamPageMaxKey*:*StreamRecord*:HashLookupMemoryTest.*:CowArrayTest.*:CowArrayDeathTest.*:ListRingTest.*:*LocalSharedPtr*'
# 249 passed.

ctest --test-dir build_debug -R '^lavik_grouped_recovery_e2e$' --output-on-failure
# All 29 recovery cases passed.

build_debug/lavik_grouped_ordered_write_e2e_test /home/ubuntu/lavik/build_debug/lavik
# 110 passed; the optional >1 GiB List case was skipped.

cmake --build build_debug --target lavik lavik_grouped_ordered_write_e2e_test lavik_grouped_recovery_e2e_test --parallel 6
build_debug/lavik_grouped_ordered_write_e2e_test /home/ubuntu/lavik/build_debug/lavik --gtest_filter='GroupedOrderedWriteE2e.ListEndSplitsWrapGrowAndRetireWithoutRewritingMiddle:GroupedOrderedWriteE2e.ListReadIntervalsAcrossPagesAndRecovery:GroupedSortedSetWriteE2e.MemberRanksSkipUnrelatedPagesAfterRecovery:GroupedSortedSetWriteE2e.ScoreBoundsHandleLongTieRunsAndMixedBatchMoves:GroupedStreamE2e.PromotesAtSharedSizeBoundaryAndRecovers:GroupedStreamE2e.AppendOnlyRewritesBoundedPagesAndRecovers:GroupedStreamE2e.DeleteRoutesIdsAndPreservesPendingAndNodeBoundaries:GroupedStreamE2e.RangeRepliesPreserveMixedSizeBinaryRecords'
# 8 passed with the final batch-capacity reservation.

/tmp/lavik-cow-array-ubsan
# 9 passed. Standalone CowArray tests compiled with GCC13 -O1
# -fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all, linked to existing Debug
# support libraries. This instruments the container templates, not all Lavik.

pre-commit run
git diff --cached --check
# Passed.
```

New coverage includes exact-size small allocations, unique/shared point updates under admission limits, unused-capacity construction, throwing-copy cleanup, over-alignment, owner-thread checks, small List recovery/growth, coordinate allocation failures with pinned snapshots, and transaction adjudication before retaining the common resident base. Existing tests exercise overlay overflow/folding, physical traversal and recovery, COW tree growth, Fenwick updates, and List wrap/growth/middle edits against vector splicing and cold recovery. The 8,193-page List test preserves middle chunks under 256 KiB of additional headroom.

The shared rank-update test also rejects malformed pages, duplicate identities and inconsistent totals across List, ZSet and Stream while preserving predecessor snapshots.

Rank fault tests verify both directions avoid unrelated endpoint pages and missing members avoid all ordered reads. Tie-run/reference-rank tests cover score moves, deletion, binary members, infinities and recovery.

### Local allocation and update measurements

Compared with PR revision 5a384914, using actual retained allocator charges on aarch64/GCC13 Debug. Directory figures include metadata, IDs, Fenwick cells and their ownership/pointer allocations, but exclude the embedded directory header and physical record index:

| Stream pages | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6,104 B | 264 B |
| 22 | 6,104 B | 3,288 B |
| 32 | 6,104 B | 4,728 B |
| 33 | 11,320 B | 5,856 B |
| 8,193 | 1,349,392 B | 1,219,272 B |

A one-page object's physical/header allocation falls from 1,424 B to 1,056 B before any coordinate override, and uses 1,144 B after a single live override.

For the allocation tradeoff, a local no-I/O microbenchmark repeatedly calls RelocateGroup with valid inline coordinates. Both the old and new object_index.cpp and the harness were compiled with `-O2`, retaining Debug assertions and linking the same Debug support libraries. Each process runs seven trials of 10,000 updates, pinned to CPU 7; three alternating old/new process pairs were run. Values below are medians of the three process medians:

| Coordinate workload | Inline overlay | Lazy overlay |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Repeatedly replace one page | 1.245 us/update | 1.727 us/update |
| Cycle eight pages (full overlay) | 1.269 us/update | 1.821 us/update |
| Cycle sixteen pages (includes folding) | 1.504 us/update | 1.934 us/update |

This measures metadata allocation/update overhead, not production command throughput or disk latency. It shows approximately 0.4–0.6 us extra work per update in this build; no end-to-end throughput claim is made.

## Risk assessment

The main correctness risks are ring wrap/rank conversion, slot reuse with pinned snapshots, incomplete local topology validation, and custom chunk alignment/lifetime/accounting. Reference comparisons, malformed-change tests, admission-failure retries, throwing-copy and over-alignment tests, UBSan checks and command/recovery tests exercise these paths.

Small arrays/objects save memory; full scalar chunks gain a header word, and hot full physical overlays gain allocation overhead. Resident metadata reduction deliberately removes only the two verified recovery-only transaction fields; type-specific bounds and version fields remain intact.

## Rollback plan

Revert the change. Ring slots, COW chunks, rank cells and resident metadata are reconstructed runtime state; existing disks require no migration.

## Reviewer guide

Start with CowArray allocation/ownership and single-chunk promotion, then OrderedGroupEntry, BuildListSlots/ApplyList and rank conversion in collection.cpp. Review GroupedPhysicalState/TryUpdatePhysicalOverrides for snapshot and failure behavior. Review the kRank path in zset.cpp for candidate-page routing. AnalyzeChanges and ReplacePages centralize common update checks and count changes; type-specific chain validation remains in ApplyList/Apply. Container, list_directory, object_index and collection tests cover the new ownership and memory invariants; ordered-write and recovery suites cover durable behavior.

## Follow-up work

None required for these changes. Arbitrary middle edits would need a different sequence representation for bounded work; further per-type metadata packing needs a separate audit of recovery and version checks.
